'''Joshua Sutton Huestis''' (born December 19, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford University]].

==Early life==
Considered a three-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Huestis was listed as the No. 48 power forward in the nation in 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=Josh Huestis Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/88510/josh-huestis|work=ESPN.com|date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> Huestis attended Charles M. Russell High School in [[Great Falls, Montana|Great Falls, MT]].

==College career==
Huestis spent four seasons at [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] and averaged 7.5 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.4 blocks in 135 career games. During both his junior and senior seasons, Huestis was named to the Pac-12 Defensive Team and at the conclusion of his sophomore season, he received Pac-12 Defensive Team Honorable Mention honors. Huestis was 2014 Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year.{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}} In 2013–14, Huestis scored in double-figures on 19 occasions while leading Stanford in rebounding (8.2 rpg) and blocks (1.9 bpg). He concluded his collegiate career as the all-time leading shot blocker in Cardinal history.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208169740 | title=#24 Josh Huestis | work=GoStanford.com | access-date=July 26, 2014 | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304100030/http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208169740 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Oklahoma City Blue (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Huestis was selected with the 29th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_draft_140626|title=Thunder Acquires Mitch McGary, Josh Huestis and Draft Rights to Semaj Christon in the 2014 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/2014draft_huestis_140702|title=Thunder Gets Diligent Worker in Huestis|work=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2014|access-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref> He later joined the Thunder for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/basketballnews/release_summer_league_2014|title=Thunder Announces Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2014|access-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref> On November 4, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/oklahomacity/training_camp_141104.html|access-date=November 4, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 4, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106170010/http://www.nba.com/dleague/oklahomacity/training_camp_141104.html|archive-date=November 6, 2014}}</ref> On November 14, he made his professional debut in a 111–105 loss to the [[Maine Red Claws]], recording 10 points, nine rebounds and two assists in 37 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|title=Babb, Taylor Spoil Christon's Oklahoma City Debut|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20141114/MNEOKL/|date=November 14, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> In 46 games for the Blue in 2014–15, he averaged 10.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.5 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Josh Huestis D-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/h/huestjo01d.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> He would not play a single game for the Thunder that season.

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2015–2018)===
On July 30, 2015, Huestis signed with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thunder Signs Josh Huestis|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/pressrelease_huestis_150730|access-date=July 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2015}}</ref> On March 24, 2016, he made his NBA debut in a 113–91 win over the [[Utah Jazz]], recording three points in five minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite news|title=Durant's 20 points lead Thunder past Jazz 113–91|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160324/UTAOKC/gameinfo.html|date=March 25, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324201426/http://www.nba.com/games/20160324/UTAOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 24, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 16, Huestis made his debut in the playoffs, recording one rebound in eight minutes off the bench in a Game 1 victory over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160416/DALOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Westbrook, Durant lead Thunder past Mavericks in Game 1|date=April 16, 2016|access-date=April 16, 2016|work=NBA.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420051641/http://www.nba.com/games/20160416/DALOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During his rookie and sophomore seasons, Huestis received multiple assignments to the Oklahoma City Blue. He was one of the first domestic draft-and-stash prospects, playing for the Blue instead of heading overseas to develop. Huestis saw a vast increase in his minutes during the 2017–18 season, playing in 69 games and becoming a regular part of the player rotation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 6, 2016|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016–17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2018–2019)===
On October 9, 2018, Huestis signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],<ref>{{cite news|title=SPURS SIGN JOSH HUESTIS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-josh-huestis|access-date=October 9, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=October 9, 2018}}</ref> but was later waived by the Spurs on October 11.<ref>{{cite news|title=SPURS WAIVE JOSH HUESTIS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-waive-josh-huestis|access-date=October 11, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=October 11, 2018}}</ref> Later Huestis was reported to have signed with their G League affiliate the [[Austin Spurs]] on October 17.<ref>{{cite news |title=Josh Huestis: Heads to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/josh-huestis-heads-to-g-league/ |access-date=October 18, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 18, 2018}}</ref> On October 22, Huestis was included in Austin's training camp roster,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2018 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018|archive-date=October 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023120939/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and on October 31, Huestis was included in Austin's opening night roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-19-opening-night-roster/|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2018–19 Opening Night Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2018|access-date=October 31, 2018|archive-date=November 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104085757/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-19-opening-night-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 31, 2019, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] acquired the returning right to Huestis from the [[Austin Spurs]] for [[Ángel Rodríguez (basketball)|Ángel Rodríguez]].<ref>{{cite web|title=VIPERS MAKE ROSTER MOVES|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-make-roster-moves|date=December 31, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 31, 2019|archive-date=January 2, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102025228/https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-make-roster-moves/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich (2019–2020)===
On July 24, 2019, [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] announced the addition of Huestis.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bayern tabs forward Huestis|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9tlrf4w4wnx48jj9/bayern-tabs-forward-huestis|date=July 24, 2019|website=euroleague.net|access-date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> On March 10, 2020, [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] parted ways with Huestis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/de/news/2019-20/03/danke-josh-huestis|title=US-Forward Huestis verlässt die Bayern-Basketballe|language=DE|date=March 10, 2020|website=fcbayern.com|access-date=March 10, 2020}}</ref>

===Cleveland Charge (2021–2022)===
On October 23, 2021, Huestis signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2021–22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}}</ref>
